operation: Precommitted all-trial fixed-score risk acceptance test for the Dots binary-reference experiment
statistic: Z=2*label*score-score^2; include every attempt, with predeclared failure score; accept only if a valid lower confidence bound for E[Z] exceeds q*36/121 plus any separately justified preparation allowance
useful_gain: Tests the scientifically relevant task risk directly and avoids treating deterministic POVM boxes as apparatus confidence. Includes failure denominators and has a direct conventional same-information comparator.
theorem_candidate: If a balanced binary experiment has only one classical failure symbol and success probability s<=1/2, even arbitrary success outcomes and label-dependent heralding have MMSE gain at most s/(1-s). Hence s>q*r^2/(1+q*r^2) is necessary for strict advantage over the ideal erasure source under that readout contract.
failure_contract_warning: The bound does not apply if failure retains additional informative classical or quantum output; Welte is nondestructive, so its missing failure instrument prevents a hardware-wide no-go.
comparator: Direct randomized bounded-loss confidence inference on exactly the same attempt records. Standard martingale/e-process theory already supplies statistical validity; novelty unestablished and no scientific capability advantage over that incumbent is claimed.
apparatus_status: NOT_ESTABLISHED; no raw calibration counts, joint confidence region, preparation calibration, or independent task trials supplied
stm_status: FROZEN_NO_GO_BURNED_TEST_UNCHANGED; no data/model refit, rescoring, acquisition, or reinterpretation of registration gap as calibrated uncertainty
